section_summary: This section contains consular reports, supervisory comments, telegrams, diplomatic despatches, and statutory translations from 1933, 1937, and 1939 regarding Japanese government shipping and shipbuilding subsidies. It opens with an extensive 1933 voluntary consular report from Kobe analyzing Japan's scrap-and-build construction bounties and route service subsidies in comparison with American and European maritime subventions, accompanied by critical commentary and budget schedules from the Supervising Consul General in Tokyo. Subsequent 1937 diplomatic correspondence between the Department of State, the Tokyo Embassy, and the Kobe Consulate concerns Japanese subsidy computations for the U.S. Maritime Commission and transmits official English translations of laws and ordinances governing fast tonnage and deep-sea navigation subsidies. The section concludes with a 1939 report examining operating subsidies and low-interest, government-guaranteed shipbuilding loans granted to Osaka Shosen Kaisha and Nippon Yusen Kaisha.

subfiles.about: A comprehensive voluntary consular report detailing Japanese government ship construction bounties, route-by-route service subsidies, and comparative international maritime subsidies.
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive report analyzes Japan's maritime subsidy policies, focusing on the 1932 Ship Construction Law scrap-and-build program and annual service subsidies paid to Japanese shipping lines across worldwide trade routes between 1930 and 1933. It highlights the strategic and commercial advantages of Japan's new fleet of high-speed diesel cargo vessels in transpacific trade while noting that Japanese service subsidies are significantly lower than American maritime subventions. Included are detailed tables of subsidized routes and operators, a world map of subsidized lines, an editorial on the World Economic Conference from the Osaka Mainichi Shimbun, capital and traffic statistics for subsidized companies, and consular source citations.
subfiles.title: Shipping Subsidies in Japan

subfiles.about: A supervisory memorandum commenting on Vice Consul McClintock's report and providing official budget and route subsidy figures for 1934-1938.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Garrels notes that Japanese subsidy figures are officially published in the budget and provides scheduled route subsidy amounts for 1934 to 1938.
subfiles.title: Comment by Supervising Consul General to Report Dated June 23, 1933, 'Shipping Subsidies in Japan' by Vice Consul Robert M. McClintock

subfiles.about: A consular criticism note directing Vice Consul McClintock to adhere to Consular Regulations regarding commentary placement in official reports.
subfiles.summary: Directs Vice Consul McClintock to place certain subjective commentary in a special attached section per Consular Regulations.
subfiles.title: Constructive Criticism Note

subfiles.about: A telegraphic instruction requesting information on Japanese ship construction and mail subsidies for U.S. Maritime Commission calculations.
subfiles.summary: Requests data on Japanese ship prices, specifications, and construction subsidies under the new law for Maritime Commission calculations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 76 to American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: A telegram transmitting preliminary information from Kobe regarding Japanese vessel prices, construction subsidies, and mail subventions.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Kobe's preliminary reply regarding unofficial ship prices, construction subsidies for combination and cargo vessels, and mail appropriations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 156 from American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting statutory expenditure limits for Japanese navigation routes, deep-sea navigation, and fast shipbuilding subsidies.
subfiles.summary: Reports maximum multi-year subsidy totals authorized for navigation routes, deep-sea navigation, and first- and second-class fast shipbuilding.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 164 from American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: An internal State Department routing notation concerning customs suggestions and shipping reporting on Japan.
subfiles.summary: Brief internal notation regarding customs suggestions and shipping reporting in Japan.
subfiles.title: Division of Trade Agreements Note on Japanese Shipping Reporting

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting Kobe Consulate Despatch No. 127 and translations of Japanese ship subsidy legislation.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Kobe Consulate Despatch No. 127 containing translations of Japanese ship subsidy legislation and budgetary figures for current subsidies.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2474, Japanese Ship Subsidy Laws

subfiles.about: A consular despatch reporting Japanese subsidy appropriations and transmitting official translations of laws and ordinances for fast tonnage and deep-sea navigation subsidies.
subfiles.summary: Consul Scott reports budgetary appropriations for Japanese navigation route, deep-sea, and fast tonnage shipbuilding subsidies, and transmits official English translations of recent maritime legislation. The enclosed laws and enforcing ordinance establish strict qualification criteria, speed formulas, domestic construction requirements, and multi-year expenditure limits for first- and second-class fast vessels and deep-sea navigation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 127, Transmission of Translation of Ship Subsidy Laws

subfiles.about: A consular report on direct operating subsidies paid to Osaka Shosen Kaisha in 1938 and indirect shipbuilding loan subsidies to Nippon Yusen Kaisha.
subfiles.summary: Reports direct government operating subsidies to Osaka Shosen Kaisha in 1938 and potential indirect subsidies through low-interest government-guaranteed shipbuilding loans.
subfiles.title: Report on Subsidies to Osaka Syosen Kaisya and Shipbuilding Financing
